judge.issues: The reviewer made three specific claims: run counts are missing, the model is unnamed, and the 200-review pilot is fabricated. The copilot did not check any of them. It should have reported, using supported / contradicted / I could not locate, that the cited sentences name no LLM and give no run count, and it should have named the sections checked. It also did not address the 200-review pilot at all. The copilot's own sentence says the paper 'reports with mean and confidence intervals', which reads like a quiet rebuttal of the reviewer's complaint. Range citations such as [S179-S210] are coarse. The opening claim that the paper 'presents two experiments' rests only on the section headings. The question uses an evaluative frame ('assess the strength'), echoes the reviewer's 'weak' framing, and bundles two topics. It is also grammatically awkward ('What, if anything, details'). There is no restatement of the reviewer's words. The reviewer's opinion was not praised or criticized, but the turn steered toward defending the results rather than giving neutral grounding.

Verdict request (novelty/accept) not explicitly declined; the turn never says the assessment is the reviewer's to make. Question is ungrammatical ('What, if anything, aspects...') and presupposes a 'Section 6' describing prior work with no cited tag. 'Richer' is a paraphrase that is not in S5 ('granular, structured, and ethically-sourced'), and S28 does not mention data. The facts largely paraphrase S4/S28 accurately. Prose is concise. The question steers toward novelty, which fits the reviewer's ask but frames comparison with prior work.
